content:
Home insurance in Moldova needs separate checks for the building, contents and potential liability to other people. A package name does not establish inclusion of all three. Before renewing for 2027, compare the existing description with the property as it is now, especially after renovation or major purchases.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. The 2027 scenarios are planning examples, not forecasts or confirmation of individual insurance terms.

Who should revisit the documents?

This review is useful for an owner completing repairs, a family buying valuable household items, a landlord and an owner whose home is financed. Lender requirements and the family's own needs may concern different objects. Identify whose property and belongings are considered and who is named as beneficiary.

List the building and fixed elements separately from furniture and appliances. For a house, identify garages, outbuildings and external equipment. An owner's policy should not automatically be described as protecting the tenant's belongings. Ask for the definition applied to each category rather than assuming everything at one address is treated alike.

Which risks and exclusions matter?

Request answers concerning fire, water damage, natural events, theft and damage caused by other people. Read exclusions alongside each risk. DONARIS’s public home-product description separates property, contents and liability. Checked 26 November 2026; it is one provider’s example, not identical terms across policies or a 2027 offer.

Ask specifically about known defects, renovation work, periods without residents and letting the home. Describe actual use, including a seasonal house. Photographs do not independently establish the cause of damage or a neighbour's responsibility; competent technical and legal assessment may be necessary.

Price, declared value and deductibles

Assessment may require the address, property characteristics, use, objects and values. Clarify the valuation basis: reconstruction of a building, interior finishes and movable contents may require different information. A property's selling price is not automatically the appropriate insured value for every component.

The premium is the price paid for insurance. The deductible is the insured's portion of a loss under the contract. This article has no verified standard tariff for every home in 2027. Compare price with item limits, valuation, deductibles and exclusions. A large overall amount does not necessarily remove a sublimit for a particular category of possessions.

The National Bank of Moldova’s contract guide explains contract components and questions for reading conditions. Checked 26 November 2026; it does not confirm a particular product, tariff or 2027 terms.

Neighbours and property used for work

Damage to your floor and a neighbour's claim are different insurance questions. Confirm whether liability is included, which people it concerns and the applicable limits. Do not promise payment on the insurer's behalf. Check notification and supporting documents in the contract actually issued.

Declare commercial stock, professional equipment or business activities at home. A residential address does not turn personal home insurance into business-property cover. Solar panels and batteries also need specific questions about components, installation and operation; a general property description does not settle them.

A practical 2027 planning example

Three situations for a practical decision

These examples are entirely hypothetical and do not describe real customers. They show what to check and which records to prepare; no risk acceptance or payment is implied.

  • Situation: Renovation has been completed. What to check: Reconcile finishes and new belongings with the previous description, valuation basis and category limits. Selling price is not automatically the appropriate amount for each insured object. Document: An updated inventory, available invoices and the existing conditions.
  • Situation: The home is let to someone else. What to check: Separate owner, tenant, their belongings and liability questions. Describe the actual occupancy rather than presenting a let property as owner-occupied. Document: The use agreement, separate inventories and an accurate occupancy description.
  • Situation: Solar panels or a battery are added to the house. What to check: Describe the system’s components and operating stage. Do not treat a general home policy as confirmation of every component or lost income. Document: The system inventory, installation or commissioning records and a written response on accepted objects.

Prepare evidence of ownership or use, an inventory, safely available photographs, value records, renovation information and the existing policy. Do not publish alarm details, serial numbers or a full valuables list. Agree confidential delivery of the information genuinely needed for assessment.

If damage occurs, people's safety comes first. Preserve relevant records and follow the applicable notification procedure; this article supplies no universal reporting deadline. The broker helps explain insurance information but does not determine the cause of a leak or make the insurer's compensation decision.

Practical prevention

Prevent administrative gaps by updating inventories and value records after renovation, retaining maintenance documentation and communicating changes in use through the contractual process. Electrical, water-system and structural problems need qualified specialists; this guide is not a repair manual.

Frequently asked questions

Which records help assess a home-insurance request?

Prepare ownership or use information, characteristics, actual use and the existing policy. Separate the building, finishes and contents, with available value records and safely obtained photographs. Keep security details and a full valuables inventory out of public forms.

Why can identical prices represent different protection?

Proposals may differ in objects, valuation, item sublimits, deductibles and liability to other people. Compare these against one accurate property description. The overall amount and a lender’s requirement do not by themselves explain all household needs.

What should I do about water damage and a neighbour’s claim?

Prioritise safety, preserve relevant records and identify the applicable documents. Check the procedures for your property and the neighbour’s allegation separately. Appropriate specialists establish cause and responsibility; do not promise compensation on the insurer’s behalf.

What needs updating after renovation or adding solar panels?

Update objects and values, describe external equipment, batteries and any changed use, and obtain a written response about what was assessed. Last year’s home policy does not automatically confirm the whole new installation for 2027.

What if the house is temporarily unoccupied?

Describe actual occupancy and ask about absence, systems and supervision under the particular conditions. This article gives neither a universal permitted absence period nor technical maintenance instructions. Resolve the relevant restrictions before treating the proposal as suitable.

Next step
